draft.title: Angles and parallel lines
card: A transversal is a line that crosses two or more other lines. When it crosses two parallel lines, it makes eight angles, and some of them are linked.
angles in matching positions at the two crossings, such as both above the line and both to the right of the transversal (an F shape). They are equal.
angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines (a Z shape). They are equal.

angles on the same side of the transversal and between the parallel lines (a C shape). They add to \(180^{\circ}\). Example: if one is \(70^{\circ}\), the other is \(180^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Parallel lines: F angles are equal, Z angles are equal, C angles add to \(180^{\circ}\).

a.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Between the lines, on the same side of the transversal, one angle is \(65^{\circ}\). What is the other angle on that side?
a.why: These are co-interior angles, which add to \(180^{\circ}\), so the other is \(180^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} = 115^{\circ}\). The answer \(65^{\circ}\) treats them as equal, which is true for corresponding and alternate angles but not co-interior angles.
a.clue: Same side and between the lines makes a C shape.

b.q: Two parallel fences are crossed by a path. One angle between the path and the upper fence is \(48^{\circ}\). The alternate angle is between the path and the lower fence. What is its size?
b.why: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal, so the angle is \(48^{\circ}\). The answer \(132^{\circ}\) comes from using the co-interior rule, which applies to angles on the same side of the path, not opposite sides.
b.clue: Alternate angles make a Z shape.

wants.brief: Two horizontal parallel lines marked with arrows, crossed by a slanted transversal. Label the eight angles at the two crossings. Show one pair of corresponding angles (F shape), one pair of alternate angles (Z shape) and one pair of co-interior angles (C shape), each pair highlighted in a different style and named.
wants.why: Seeing the F, Z and C shapes on one diagram helps students spot each type of angle pair.
